title: GitLab MCP Server
summary: Work with GitLab issues, merge requests and pipelines from your agent through the MCP server built into GitLab itself.
description: GitLab ships an MCP server inside the product, at /api/v4/mcp on your instance. An agent can read issues and merge requests, look at repository files and check CI pipelines, using the permissions of the account that signed in.

This config points at gitlab.com. For a self-managed instance, change the host. Your group owner (on GitLab.com) or administrator (self-managed) has to allow MCP server access first. Sign-in uses OAuth, so no token is stored in the config.
useWhen: Summarize a merge request and its review threads
List the issues assigned to you this sprint
Find out why a merge request pipeline failed
Open an issue from a bug you just found

mcp.name: gitlab
access: Reads projects, issues, merge requests, repository files and pipelines your account can see
Can create or update issues and merge requests where your account has rights

example.prompt: Summarize merge request !482 in the web project and tell me whether its pipeline is green.
example.result: !482 "Paginate the audit log" has 2 unresolved threads, both about the page size default. The latest pipeline passed on all 6 jobs, 12 minutes ago.

faq.question: Why do I get a 403 error?
faq.answer: GitLab rejects legacy personal and project tokens here. Use the OAuth sign-in, or a fine-grained token with the MCP Execute permission.

faq.question: Does it work on a self-managed instance?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace gitlab.com in the URL with your host, and have an administrator enable MCP access for the instance.

faq.question: Can I limit what it exposes?
faq.answer: GitLab groups tools into toolsets and lets you choose them with a request header. Defaults cover core, merge requests, work items, repository and CI.

access: Acts with the permissions of the signed-in GitLab user
